turns.text: ABHA number vs ABHA address, whats the difference and which one should I save as the patient id in my HMIS?

must_contain: The ABHA number is a unique 14 digit identifier issued after identity verification, and the patient record should key on it.
The ABHA address is a readable identifier in the form user@abdm that routes records, and it is what care contexts are linked to and consent requests are raised against.
One ABHA number can carry more than one ABHA address and the person can add more later, so an address stored as the primary key breaks.
notes: The two ABHA identifiers are the most confused pair in M1. The wrong-sibling literals ban describing the address as the 14 digit value. Source lines: catalogue/hiecm/concepts/abha-number-and-address.md, 'The ABHA Number is a unique 14-digit identifier assigned to an individual after successful identity verification'; 'The ABHA Address is a unique and user-friendly identifier in the format: `user@abdm`'; 'The address answers where their records are routed, and it is the identifier care contexts are linked to and consent requests are raised against. One number can carry more than one address'; 'Your patient record keys on the ABHA number, because a person can hold several addresses and add more later'; 'An address stored as the primary key breaks when the person adds or changes one.' Review: must_not_contain 'abha address is a 14' removed: the default ABHA address is built from the 14 digits, so a correct answer can match it.
